title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits & perks, hiring & onboarding, internal tools
author: Alexandra Chen
content:
Introduction

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook section describing what it means to work at Redwood: our expectations, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding lifecycle, and primary internal tools new employees need to know. It is intended for new hires, managers, interviewers, and cross-functional partners.

1) Working at Redwood — our culture and expectations

Summary: Redwood is engineering- and customer-centric with a bias toward production reliability, developer experience, and measurable impact. We value clear communication, ownership, and pragmatic decision-making.

Core behaviors we expect from every Redwoder:
- Ship thoughtful work quickly and iterate based on data.
- Communicate asynchronously and document decisions in Confluence.
- Be customer-obsessed: prioritize reliability and cost-consciousness for inference at scale.
- Coach, mentor, and raise the bar for peers.
- Practice security-minded design and follow our secure SDLC.

Working models and time off
- Default working model: hybrid. Teams define core collaboration days with manager agreement.
- PTO: unlimited discretionary policy with guideline minimum of 20 days per year for full-time employees. Use the HR portal to log time off.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers, 8 weeks for secondary caregivers; flexible return-to-work schedule is supported.
- Sick leave and caregiver leave provided per local statutory requirements and enhanced company policy where applicable.

2) Roles & career ladders (overview)

Scope: This section summarizes role families and leveling principles. For detailed leveling matrices and compensation bands see the separate leveling guides linked in related pages.

Role families at Redwood (examples)
- Engineering: IC (SWE I / II), Senior SWE, Staff SWE, Senior Staff / Principal; Engineering Managers (EM I / II / Director); SRE, Platform, Runtime engineers.
- Product: PM I / II / Senior PM / Lead PM / Group PM.
- Design & Research: Designer, Senior Designer, Lead.
- Applied ML & Evals: ML Engineer, Applied Researcher, Model Operations.
- GTM: Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering.
- Core functions: People Ops, Finance, Legal, Security, Marketing.

Leveling principles (high level)
1. Impact: scope of projects, cross-team influence, and business outcomes.
2. Complexity: technical difficulty, ambiguity, and stakeholder management.
3. Autonomy: degree of independent execution and mentoring.
4. Scope: number of direct reports (for managers), product/service ownership, and team's operational impact.

Typical expectations by ladder (short):
- SWE II / Senior SWE: writes solid production code, owns features end-to-end, participates in design reviews, mentors juniors.
- Staff SWE: leads cross-team technical initiatives, sets service-level tradeoffs, shapes architecture and operational practices.
- Engineering Manager I: delivers team outcomes, runs effective 1:1s, handles hiring and performance management.
- Principal/Senior Staff: company-level technical leadership, defines platform strategy, and represents Redwood in public technical forums.

Promotion and calibration process
- Frequency: formal promotion cycles twice per year with mid-cycle exceptions for exceptional cases.
- Process: manager compiles evidence (OKRs, project summaries, 360 feedback), submits to calibration panel, HR and People Ops validate compensation and level alignment.
- Evidence checklist: documented project summary, impact metrics (latency/cost improvements, reliability wins), peer reviews, and manager narrative.

3) Benefits & perks (high level)

Health & financial
- Medical, dental, and vision plans for employees and dependents with company contribution tiers by region.
- 401(k) / pension or country-equivalent retirement plan with company match where applicable.
- Equity: standard grant at hire with recurring refresh grants for tenured employees; details in offer letter.

Time, family & wellness
- Generous PTO and paid holidays.
- Parental leave (see section above).
- Wellness stipend: $/month stipend for health and well-being activities.
- Mental health coverage and EAP (employee assistance program).

Learning & growth
- Learning stipend: $1,500/year (pro-rated) for books, courses, and conferences. Manager approval required for conference travel.
- Internal learning: regular lunch-and-learns, engineering brown-bags, and a mentorship program coordinated by People Ops.

Work setup & allowances
- Equipment: standard MacBook or Linux laptop, external monitor stipend, and ergonomic accessories.
- Home office stipend for remote-first employees and travel support for on-site days.

Perks & discretionary programs
- Commuter allowance where applicable.
- Team offsites and town halls.
- Volunteer time off (4 days/year) and donation matching program.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

High-level recruiting lifecycle
1. Requisition: Hiring manager opens req in Greenhouse (or agreed ATS); People Ops reviews and posts role-specific job description.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter screens candidates; initial phone screen with hiring manager or recruiter.
3. Interviews: interview loop typically includes take-home exercise (if applicable), technical interviews, system design, role-specific practicals, and a cross-functional partner interview (e.g., SRE/product).
4. Debrief: Interviewers submit feedback in the ATS; hiring manager schedules calibration and debrief with recruiter and People Ops.
5. Offer: Recruiter extends verbal offer and follows with written offer letter; People Ops coordinates background checks and reference checks where required.
6. Acceptance & pre-boarding: HR creates account provisioning plan and schedules first-week onboarding.

Interview best practices for interviewers
- Use the rubric provided in the interview guide. Rate against leveling criteria, not against a hypothetical perfect candidate.
- Provide concrete feedback with examples and highlight risk areas.
- Prioritize diverse interview panels and avoid undisclosed personal questions.

New hire onboarding checklist (first 30 days)
- Pre-start: SSO/Okta account created, hardware shipped, onboarding calendar shared.
- Day 1: Welcome session, People Ops overview, IT account setup (GitHub, Slack, Confluence, CI/CD access).
- Week 1: Team onboarding (team goals, pairing sessions), security training, and compliance signoffs.
- Month 1: Deliver a small onboarding project, meet cross-functional partners, set 30/60/90 day goals with manager.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Prepare onboarding plan before start date.
- Assign a buddy for the first 30 days.
- Schedule regular 1:1 cadence and initial expectations/goal-setting meeting.

5) Internal tools guide (quick start & links)

Account & access basics
- Single Sign-On (SSO / Okta): primary authentication. Use Okta multi-factor authentication (MFA) and register a backup method.
- VPN & corporate network: use the VPN client for private deployments and internal-only services. Follow the eng-infra runbooks for access.

Primary collaboration tools
- Slack: main day-to-day communication. Channels are organized by team, product area, and initiatives. Use threads and emoji reactions for lightweight async signals.
- Confluence: canonical docs live here—create pages under the appropriate space and follow the Confluence page template.
- GitHub: source of truth for code. Branching, PR, and CI rules are enforced via CODEOWNERS and CI pipelines.
- CI/CD: Jenkins/Buildkite (team-dependent). Pipelines are documented; ensure you have the correct deploy permissions before attempting a production rollout.

Observability & incident tooling
- Datadog: dashboards and alerts. Dashboards are owned at the service level (see eng-platform dashboards-and-alerts).
- PagerDuty: on-call rotations and escalation. On-call runbooks are stored in confluence/runbooks.
- Sentry/bug tracker: application errors and exceptions. Link issues to retrospectives when incidents occur.

Security, secrets & keys
- Vault/KMS: secrets storage for production keys; developers should not commit credentials to Git. See security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth for access procedures.
- Key rotation: follow the four-step rotation playbook in security-and-compliance.

Developer & product tooling specific to Redwood
- Redwood Console (internal staging): use for testing API routes, inspecting request traces, and debugging model routing. Access controlled via Okta groups.
- Dedicated admin portal: reserved capacity and customer config management. Use only with manager approval for customer-impacting actions.
- Local dev: prescriptive dev environment via devkit (docker / nvidia runtime for GPU tests). Typical commands:
  - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/devkit.git
  - make dev-up  # starts local services, see README for options

6) How we measure success (people & performance)

Performance cycles and feedback
- Cadence: quarterly check-ins and an annual performance review. Managers should run mid-quarter 1:1s and document progress against OKRs.
- 360 feedback: peers and cross-functional partners provide input during review windows.

Manager expectations for continuous development
- Run clear goal setting and calibration meetings.
- Provide regular, timely feedback and career discussions.
- Sponsor team members for visibility and cross-team opportunities.

7) Templates and quick references (appendix)

Sample 30/60/90 goals (engineer)
- 30 days: Understand the runtime and get a local dev environment running; fix a small bug or implement a small feature.
- 60 days: Own a medium-sized ticket, contribute to a service-level dashboard, and ship a customer-facing tweak.
- 90 days: Lead a small cross-team project and present results to the team.

Promotion evidence checklist (copyable)
- Project summary (one paragraph)
- Key metrics (latency, cost, error rate, revenue impact)
- Cross-team feedback (2–3 quotes or bullet points)
- Mentoring and leadership examples

Security & compliance reminders
- Complete required security training within the first week.
- Follow data residency requirements for customer data and use customer isolation features for Private deployments.

Related pages and further reading
- Leveling guides and compensation bands (see related pages).
- On-call and incident response runbooks in eng-sre.
- Security onboarding checklist in security-and-compliance.

Ownership and updates
- Document owner: People Ops (Alexandra Chen).
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner for major policy changes.
- For corrections or additions: open a PR to this page in Confluence or contact People Ops at people-ops@redwood.ai.
